newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil debt growing too fast - IADB's Hausmann.
newsitem.headline: Brazil debt growing too fast - IADB's Hausmann.

text.p: Brazil's external accounts are healthy but the growth in internal debt is of concern, said Ricardo Hausmann, chief economist at the Inter-American Development Bank (IADB).

Hausmann, speaking to Reuters late Monday at a seminar on public finance, said Latin American countries should not evaluate their debt stock in terms of Gross Domestic Product but in terms of the size of their financial systems.
"We would like to see Brazil accumulate debt at a much lower speed than it is currently doing," Hausmann said.
"On fiscal matters we tend to defer to the International Monetary Fund. But we believe it is better to err on the side of prudence," he said.
Hausmann said Brazil needed room for fiscal manouevre if its economic stabilization plan were to remain on track.
"It would be helpful if (fiscal) adjustments could be made sooner rather than later," he said.

He said that even though the government was working on the long-term solutions to its fiscal problems, mainly through reforms passing through Congress, it was important in the short run that the growth in internal debt did not speed up.
Brazil's net public sector debt in June stood at 33.9 percent of GDP, with net internal debt of 210.7 billion reais reaching 29.6 percent of GDP.
Hausmann said it was wrong to compare Latin American economies with countries like Italy, where the debt stock stands at something like 120 percent of GDP.
Italy's debt amounted to three years worth of tax receipts, he noted, and its financial system was much larger.
"Brazil's tax base is big but it also has a small financial system," he said.
The IADB economist praised Brazil's plan to salvage state-owned banks through special credit lines tied to deregulation programmes.
"I think they are acting with great prudence. But the most important thing is the separation of state banks from government," he said.
